pairs: De iis autem quæ idolis sacrificantur,
Now concerning those things that are sacrificed to idols:
we know that we all have knowledge.
Si quis autem se existimat scire aliquid,
But if anyone considers himself to know anything,
nondum cognovit quemadmodum oporteat eum scire.
he does not yet know in the way that he ought to know.
De escis autem quæ idolis immolantur,
But as to the foods that are immolated to idols,
scimus quia nihil est idolum in mundo,
we know that an idol in the world is nothing,
and that no one is God,
Nam etsi sunt qui dicantur dii sive in cælo,
For although there are things that are called gods,
sive in terra (siquidem sunt dii multi,
whether in heaven or on earth,
(if one even considers there to be many gods and many lords)
yet we know that there is only one God,
Sed non in omnibus est scientia.
But knowledge is not in everyone.
Quidam autem cum conscientia usque nunc idoli,
For some persons, even now, with consent to an idol,
eat what has been sacrificed to an idol.
et conscientia ipsorum cum sit infirma,
Esca autem nos non commendat Deo.
Yet food does not commend us to God.
and if we do not eat,
Videte autem ne forte hæc licentia vestra offendiculum fiat infirmis.
But be careful not to let your liberty become a cause of sin to those who are weak.
Si enim quis viderit eum, qui habet scientiam, in idolio recumbentem:
For if anyone sees someone with knowledge sitting down to eat in idolatry,
cum sit infirma, ædificabitur ad manducandum idolothyta?
being infirm, be emboldened to eat what has been sacrificed to idols?
Et peribit infirmus in tua scientia, frater,
And should an infirm brother perish by your knowledge,
even though Christ died for him?
So when you sin in this way against the brothers,
and you harm their weakened conscience,
Quapropter si esca scandalizat fratrem meum,
Because of this, if food leads my brother to sin,
lest I lead my brother to sin.
